description: Provider-opaque scenarios for validating reusable Hub invariants across domains.

scenarios.purpose: Two independently deployed A2A Providers exchange Tasks and Artifacts through one tenant-scoped Hub.
hubInvariants: provider internals remain opaque
remote task and context identifiers are preserved
a branch failure does not erase successful branches
task and artifact state is tenant scoped

scenarios.purpose: A real independently maintained Provider and a separate fixture use the same Hub contract.
hubInvariants: Provider framework and model API are not visible to the Hub
AgentCard is the capability boundary
remote provenance survives reconciliation
scenarios.evidence: local real-provider smoke; requires ca-agent and configured credentials

scenarios.purpose: Three independently deployed domain-labelled Providers use skill routing, Artifacts, HITL continuation, and tenant isolation through one Hub.
hubInvariants: domain-specific AgentCards are the only routing input
remote Task and Context IDs remain opaque
HITL continuation does not expose provider internals
tenant state is isolated

scenarios.purpose: A Go SDK Provider and a Python SDK Provider use one Hub without exposing runtime-specific implementation state.
hubInvariants: AgentCard and A2A are the only integration boundary
remote IDs survive continuation
runtime-specific behavior remains Provider-owned
a stopped branch does not affect the other runtime
scenarios.evidence: repository-owned Go and Python SDK process fixtures

scenarios.purpose: Long-running implementation, review, sandbox Artifacts, approval, and restart recovery.
hubInvariants: execution checkpoints remain Provider-owned
Hub resumes by remote Task and Context IDs
side-effecting Artifacts have durable provenance

scenarios.purpose: Cross-organization identity, delegated approval, payment intent, audit, and compensation.
hubInvariants: tenant and delegated identity are auditable
failed side effects expose compensation state
no Provider receives another Provider's private state

scenarios.purpose: Parallel research fan-out/fan-in with evidence Artifacts, partial failure, and provenance.
hubInvariants: fan-in retains branch-level status
evidence Artifacts retain source identity
one unavailable Provider does not cancel unrelated work

scenarios.purpose: Event-triggered investigation, priority, retries, bounded remediation, and cancellation.
hubInvariants: event delivery is at-least-once and deduplicated
remediation requires explicit policy
cancellation intent is observable

scenarios.purpose: Multimodal Artifact production, evaluation loops, and publishing side effects.
hubInvariants: MIME and size policy is domain-neutral
Artifact identity is content-addressed
publishing remains an explicit Provider side effect

scenarios.purpose: Offline or mailbox-connected Agents continue work across identity and channel boundaries.
hubInvariants: AAMP mailbox correlation maps to the common Task model
offline delivery does not change tenant ownership
replayed messages are idempotent

scenarios.purpose: Real-time streams, tool calls, safety policy, and bounded physical side effects.
hubInvariants: safety policy is evaluated before side effects
stream disconnects are recoverable without duplicate commands
tool outputs remain observable but opaque

scenarios.purpose: Dynamic discovery, trust, pricing, quotas, and untrusted participant isolation.
hubInvariants: discovery does not imply trust
quota and authorization are tenant/subject scoped
untrusted AgentCards cannot expand Hub authority
